title: Estimating heterogeneous impacts Of subsidised health insurance: A causal machine learning approach
summary: Causal-forest analysis of a nationally representative Indonesian survey estimated heterogeneous associations between subsidized JKN insurance and healthcare use. Average utilization was higher among insured respondents, while estimated outpatient participation effects were negative for about one-fifth of the sample. The cross-sectional observational design relies on measured covariates and does not establish randomized causal effects.
ai_technology: Causal forests estimate heterogeneous treatment effects; super-learner nuisance models and a two-part outcome model separate seeking care from care consumed. Sample splitting, cross-fitting, and doubly robust scores are used.
organization: Centre for Health Economics, University of York, York, England, United Kingdom; The CHOICE Institute, School of Pharmacy, University of Washington, Seattle, Washington, United States of America

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Causal forests, cross-fitting and doubly robust scores were applied to 912,812 respondents in the 2017 SUSENAS survey.
evidence.unknown: Observational estimates depend on measured-confounder assumptions and do not establish effects under random assignment.
